linkedin.hook: Why pooled lending risk fails institutional capital on Soroban.
linkedin.copy:
Most money market wrappers on newer execution environments rely on pooled vaults. When a borrower defaults on an illiquid collateral position, every liquidity provider absorbs the haircut. Blend v2 b-tokens solve asset-level isolation, but managing them programmatically still exposes lenders to cross-account contamination if the intermediate architecture aggregates custody.

Vanna approaches Soroban credit through dedicated SmartAccounts rather than commingled pool contracts. Each account operates as an isolated state machine with a strict 1.10x Health Factor floor. By reading state directly through a ~320ms Mercury indexer pipeline, the liquidation engine triggers targeted partial liquidations for 0.00014 XLM fixed gas without freezing liquidity or affecting external balances.

Non-custodial leverage infrastructure should never ask capital allocators to underwrite unknown counterparty liabilities. We have pushed this architecture to Soroban testnet so teams can evaluate isolated b-token credit loops before mainnet deployment. Deploy your testnet SmartAccount sandbox at test.stellar.vanna.finance.

reddit.hook: How we integrated Blend v2 b-tokens into non-custodial Soroban SmartAccounts (technical breakdown)
reddit.copy:
We spent the last few weeks implementing Blend v2 pool mechanics on Soroban testnet, specifically focused on eliminating counterparty spillover for active yield positions.

The standard approach in DeFi lending aggregation is to deploy a shared vault contract that holds b-tokens on behalf of all depositors. If one user's position becomes insolvent during extreme market volatility, the entire vault takes a loss. We rejected that model.

Instead, Vanna spins up an isolated Soroban SmartAccount for each trader. The SmartAccount interacts directly with Blend v2 pool contracts, minting and burning b-tokens while leaving ownership and custody solely with the user. The contract enforces a hard 1.10x Health Factor floor. Because we index pool states with ~320ms Mercury latency, our off-chain keepers evaluate margin requirements in near real time. If a position drops below the threshold, liquidations execute directly against that isolated SmartAccount for roughly 0.00014 XLM fixed gas. Other positions in the protocol remain completely untouched.

You can test this contract setup directly on Stellar testnet right now. Initialize your isolated account, supply test assets into Blend pools, and test margin parameters without commingling assets. Deploy your testnet SmartAccount sandbox at test.stellar.vanna.finance.

Disclosure: I am part of the core dev team at Vanna Protocol building credit infrastructure on Stellar Soroban.
